title: Ordinary finite-type conormal cohomology is ideal-power torsion on an etale complement
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $H\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $C$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(H)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Choose any surjective $A$-algebra map $\alpha:A[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\to C$ with $s\geq0$ finite and kernel $K$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $d_\alpha:K/K^2\to C^{\oplus s}$, $f\bmod K^2\mapsto(\alpha(\partial f/\partial y_j))_j$. Its kernel $M_1$ and cokernel $M_0$ are finitely generated $C$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There exists $b\geq0$ such that $H^bM_1=H^bM_0=0$, where every element of $H^b$ acts through $A\to C$.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), proof: finiteness of ordinary naive cotangent cohomology and annihilation from etaleness over the complement. Tag 0AKA (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, uses exactly these finite power-torsion cohomology modules before completing them.

proof.text: Write $P=A[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$. The differential in the statement is well-defined: if $u,v\in K$, every coordinate of $d(uv)$ is $\alpha(u)\alpha(\partial v)+\alpha(v)\alpha(\partial u)=0$. Thus differentiation followed by $\alpha$ kills $K^2$. For $p\in P$ and $f\in K$, the Leibniz rule gives $d(pf)=\alpha(p)d(f)$, so the resulting map is $C=P/K$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), partial derivations and Leibniz rule; Section 00S0 (section-netherlander), presentation differential

proof.text: Both $P$ and $C$ are finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence Noetherian. Choose ideal generators $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ of $K$, using the definition of Noetherian. Their classes generate $K/K^2$ over $C$: in $f=\sum p_i k_i$ reduce each coefficient $p_i$ modulo $K$. The Noetherian submodule theorem over $C$ now makes $M_1\subseteq K/K^2$ finitely generated. The images of the $s$ coordinate vectors generate $M_0=C^{\oplus s}/\operatorname{im}(d_\alpha)$. This proves both finiteness assertions.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), second assertion; used in restricted.tex Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), first paragraph

proof.text: Choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $H$, possible since $A$ is Noetherian. Fix one generator $a=a_j$ and let $g$ be its image in $C$. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(H)$ and $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$ for $f:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. By hypothesis $X_U\to U$ is etale. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ induced by $C\to C_g$ is an open immersion with image $D(g)$ (principal-localization open immersion), and the affine basic-open/localization statement identifies the open subscheme $D(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_g$; composing with $f$, the morphism $D(g)\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the one induced by $A\to C\to C_g$. Every prime avoiding $g$ contracts to a prime avoiding $a\in H$, hence $D(g)\subseteq X_U$. Restrict $X_U\to U$ to this open using etale open restriction. The inclusion $U\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale and etale morphisms compose, so $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale.

proof.text: Apply the principal-localization presentation theorem to $\alpha$, $g$, and the constant lift $a\in P$. It gives a surjection $\beta:P[z]\to C_g$, $z\mapsto g^{-1}$, with kernel $J=(K,az-1)$. This ideal is finitely generated by the generators of $K$ from Step 2 and $az-1$, so the etale conormal criterion applies to $\beta$. By Step 3 its conormal differential $d_\beta$ is bijective. The polynomial differential basis identifies the differential of $\alpha$ with $d_\alpha$ in coordinates. The cited presentation theorem decomposes the localized presentation complex as $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)\cong\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)_g\oplus(C_g\xrightarrow{g}C_g)$. Since $g$ is a unit, the second differential is bijective; the direct-sum decomposition therefore shows that $(d_\alpha)_g$ is bijective as well.

source.place: Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), parts (1)-(3); Tag 00U1 (definition-etale), with presentation comparison Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy); Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring)

proof.text: Localization is exact. Apply it to $0\to M_1\to K/K^2\xrightarrow{d_\alpha}C^{\oplus s}$ and to $K/K^2\xrightarrow{d_\alpha}C^{\oplus s}\to M_0\to0$, localizing at $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots\}$. Exactness identifies $(M_1)_g$ with the kernel of $(d_\alpha)_g$ and $(M_0)_g$ with its cokernel (the maps on fractions send $x/g^n$ to its usual image divided by $g^n$). Step 4 makes both zero. This applies separately to every generator $a_j$ of $H$.

For each $j$ and $i\in\{0,1\}$, apply the finite-module localization-zero annihilator theorem over $C$ to $M_i$ and the powers of $g_j$, where $g_j$ is the image of $a_j$. Its hypotheses are Step 2 (finite generation) and Step 5 (zero localization). It gives $n_{j,i}\geq0$ with $g_j^{n_{j,i}}M_i=0$. Set $e_j=\max(1,n_{j,0},n_{j,1})$. Then $a_j^{e_j}$ acts as zero on both $M_0$ and $M_1$ through $A\to C$.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), converse paragraph; exercises.tex Tag 076A (exercise-localize-finite-module-zero); smoothing.tex Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma) uses a single annihilator for a finite localized-zero module

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $H=0$ and $b=1$ works. Otherwise set $b=1+\sum_{j=1}^r(e_j-1)$. The ideal $H^b$ is generated by the monomials $a_1^{v_1}\cdots a_r^{v_r}$ with $\sum v_j=b$: this follows by expanding a product of $b$ linear combinations of the generators of $H$. In each such monomial some $v_j\geq e_j$, since otherwise $\sum v_j\leq\sum(e_j-1)=b-1$. That monomial is divisible by $a_j^{e_j}$ and therefore kills both modules by Step 6. Sums and $A$-multiples still kill them, so $H^bM_1=H^bM_0=0$, as required.
